title: Universal scaling and relaxation in decaying turbulence of Bose gases
authors: Arnol D. García-Orozco, Michelle A. Moreno-Armijos, Sarah Sab, Amilson Fritsch, Vanderlei Salvador Bagnato
abstract: Understanding the relaxation dynamics of isolated quantum systems remains a central challenge in nonequilibrium physics. In this short review, we discuss recent experimental and theoretical advances in universal dynamics of turbulent Bose gases, with particular emphasis on nonthermal fixed points and wave turbulence in our experimental system at the São Carlos Institute of Physics of the University of São Paulo. We highlight the emergence of self-similar scaling behavior and its connection to particle and energy transport across momentum scales. In addition, we discuss an approach in which a differential equation has a universal scaling solution, providing a practical framework for extracting universal exponents from limited regions of the momentum distribution. Furthermore, we recap experimental observations of direct and inverse cascades in a three-dimensional trapped Bose--Einstein condensate, revealing distinct relaxation stages governed by universal scaling laws. These results demonstrate that turbulence plays a key role in far-from-equilibrium dynamics, offering a unified perspective on transport processes and thermalization in quantum many-body systems.
summary: This review and study investigates how turbulent Bose gases relax far from equilibrium by analyzing universal scaling laws. The authors combine theory (NTFPs, WKE) with experiments on BECs to show that the decay proceeds through distinct direct and inverse cascade stages. This confirms turbulence's role in establishing universal transport dynamics in quantum many-body systems.
main_problem: The central challenge is understanding the relaxation dynamics of isolated quantum systems, particularly how far-from-equilibrium evolution in turbulent Bose gases can be described by universal scaling laws.
main_result: The system exhibits self-similar evolution characterized by Nonthermal Fixed Points (NTFPs), demonstrating distinct direct and inverse cascade stages governed by universal power-law exponents ($\alpha$ and $ eta$).
method: The study combines theoretical analysis using weak kinetic equations, renormalization group concepts, and differential equation approaches with experimental measurements of momentum distributions via Time-of-Flight imaging.
model_or_system: The system under investigation is a Bose gas (e.g., $^{87}	ext{Rb}$ BEC) driven into a turbulent, far-from-equilibrium state using controlled excitation potentials in an ultracold atomic trap.
key_observables: Momentum distribution $n(k, t)$, average particle number ($N$), and mean kinetic energy ($\langle k^2 angle$).
important_parameters: Universal scaling exponents ($\alpha$ and $ eta$), momentum scales (UV/IR limits), and time evolution relative to characteristic times ($t/t_0$).
main_assumptions: The emergence of universal dynamical scaling despite different microscopic interactions, and the applicability of simplified differential equations in specific momentum regimes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the collapse of momentum distributions into single universal functions after rescaling for both direct (depletion) and inverse (repopulation) cascades. One figure shows the time evolution of low-momentum states ($n(k 	o 0, t)$) validating scaling laws.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the theoretical framework using weak kinetic equations and NTFP concepts to detailing experimental measurements that confirm self-similar scaling. It then presents alternative analytical methods (differential equations) to extract universal exponents ($\alpha$ and $ eta$) from limited data regions, confirming consistency across different analysis techniques.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete realization of non-equilibrium statistical mechanics in an ultracold atomic setting, linking fundamental concepts like wave turbulence and universality classes to measurable physical observables in quantum gases.

Fig. 4 (a) Momentum distributions of a turbulent state for an excitation amplitude A = 2.2µ0 at different holding times t. The universal exponents that described beaviour are α = −0.50(8) and β = −0.2(4). The vertical dashed line indicates the infrared cutoff ks, delimiting the momentum range where the scaling described by Eq. 8 holds. Reproduced from Ref. [33].

Fig. 5 Global quantities, as defined in Eqs. 9 and 10, for the excitation amplitudes of A = 1.8µ0. The shaded region corresponds to the time window in which universal behavior is observed. The left axis shows the total number of particles, N, and the universality range (ks ≤7µm−1) as a function of t. The mean kinetic energy M2 (right axis) increases with time within the same universal range. The curves follow the theoretical predictions, namely, N ∝ tα−2β and M2 ∝t−2β. Reproduced from Ref. [33].
